subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Wug Test
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Wug Test.

hook.text: "This is a wug. Now there are two of them. There are two…" The child says "wugs." She applied the rule.

buildup.text: Jean Berko Gleason's 1958 test proved children extract grammar rules, not just memorized forms.

discovery.text: Kids applied plural (-s), past tense (-ed), and possessive (-'s) to words they'd never heard.

twist.text: Errors like "goed" and "mouses" are signs of progress—they prove the child learned a rule.

climax.text: The wug test is one of the most replicated studies in linguistics. Grammar is rule-based.

punchline.text: Kids don't memorize language. They crack it.

quiz.question: What did the Wug Test demonstrate?
options: Children apply grammar rules to novel words
Children only memorize words they hear
Grammar is taught explicitly by parents
